pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Track ownership of scale subresource for all scalable resources i.e. Deployment, ReplicaSet, StatefulSet, ReplicationController, and Custom Resources.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #82046
Fixes #94585

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
I opened https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/95921 as an initial attempt to solve the problem. As this PR follows a different approach, I decided to open a new PR for clarity.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
Track ownership of scale subresource for all scalable resources i.e. Deployment, ReplicaSet, StatefulSet, ReplicationController, and Custom Resources.
```

issue_context.title: Server-side Apply: Ownership not tracked for scale subresource
issue_context.body: Whenever someone sends a scale sub-resources request, the managed fields are not changed for that specific request, which means that the scale will typically not grab the ownership of the "replicas" field. This is obviously a bug, but we don't exactly know how to fix it for now.
comments: /sig api-machinery
/cc @lavalamp @jennybuckley @kwiesmueller
I would have expected we fix this by turning a request to /scale into a corresponding request against the main resource and running through the ordinary code?
A *large* motivator for apply as a feature is letting robots manage spec.replicas, which is the purpose of /scale. So, this is not a small bug.

@lavalamp I think that's the right way to fix it, but it's not how scale subresource works now. I think a request to deployments/scale, for example, doesn't go through all the normal admission for deployments

Yes, webhooks and validation are done on the scale objects, not the final/"patched" object, which I found a little confusing too: 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/apps/deployment/storage/storage.go#L272-L320
There still exists a "new" deployment object, though: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/apps/deployment/storage/storage.go#L300
Yeah, we might be able to address this bug specifically by updating the managed fields there somehow

If we write a single field manager named `/scale` to storage such that it takes ownership of `.spec.replicas`, then any `kubectl apply`s would conflict if they attempt to take ownership of `.spec.replicas` as intended.

Also, the HorizontalPodAutoscaler and a user can share ownership of `.spec.replicas` w/ `kubectl scale`. Is this the intended behavior, or do we want `kubectl scale` to conflict?
Setting `.spec.replicas` via scale should be exactly the same as setting it by using the main endpoint, conflicts and all.

We could use the same mechanism proposed in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/923 to declare the field manager on the scale subresource.

If we expect scale to produce a conflict, then ideally we do use a server-side apply.

Will users eventually receive conflicts for [other imperative `kubectl` commands like `kubectl scale`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/manage-kubernetes-objects/imperative-command/#how-to-update-objects)?

To be clear. Using scale via PUT or non-apply patch should not produce a conflict. It should force, causing the folks APPLYing to the base resource (or APPLYing to scale) to get a conflict.

I'd expect `kubectl scale` to force and never give a conflict; you'd get a conflict when you subsequently tried to APPLY and own the `.spec.replicas` field.

Make sense?
Ahhh yes

Is it really right to not go through, say, the regular deployment mutating admission/webhooks when someone modifies a deployment through `/scale`? Because that seems to be the current behavior.

For example, if I made a mutating webhook which maintains a label on deployments based on the replica count, it wouldn't work since someone could get around it by doing a `/scale`

No, that is a bug, I think.

I think it's a bug too, but we already [support](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/#request) making, say, a `deployment/scale` webhook, which looks at the `autoscaling/v1.Scale` being sent to that endpoint. So if we wanted to fix this for admission in general, I think we would have to call both the scale admission chain and then the regular admission chain.

Not sure if that's feasible, or if we should just do what @apelisse was suggesting in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/82046#issuecomment-525930084 and just do the managed fields update (since it's just for the one field)

Seems lower priority, but I think we'd want to track a TODO somewhere for similar changes for updating the manager for /scale on CRDs

review_comments: Instead of constructing a scale object from the existing deployment, I expected us to construct a deployment object from the new scale object and the existing deployment object, and apply or update that?
doesn't the `patch` path have to work in terms of the request object?

This is more or less what's happening. The problem is that in order to get the new scale object we need the "old scale" object from the deployment and run it through [UpdatedObject](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/apps/deployment/storage/storage.go#L378). UpdatedObject will update the managed fields of the scale object and conflict if needed.
I think I am objecting to a large part of the existing codebase here. Antoine attempted to convince me that I have to hold my nose for this. I'll look again.
Maybe special treat the case where `path` is `nil` here, so that you conserve the entry without ever stealing anything from it.

Yes much better.

At first I excluded to use `nil` because I didn't want to enforce `Path` to be something "nullable", e.g. if we want to change it to a struct in the future. I think it's OK to use nil for now though :-) 

I force-pushed here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/6c86e89390e262cc54be647bc09328a4d8d654fb

It's a little unfortunate that we won't be able to find the replicas field in versions that don't have the "Scale" sub-resource. I guess it's fine to mostly just ignore this and assume they don't have it.
But is the scale handler going to gently ignore these, or is it going to remove their entire entry?
We absolutely have to fix that.

That's a good point. 

A possible solution would be for the scale handler to always ignore entries with version it doesn't know about, instead of dropping. This would apply for both CRs and other resources.  That would be inconsistent with `Apply`, I think.

Another way would be to somehow limit this behaviour to CRs, by passing some parameter down to the scale handler, so that we have a different logic for custom resources. I am not sure I like that though.
I think there is a difference between versions that don't exist and versions that don't have a scale subresource.

Right, what about https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/98377/commits/1f1d9387ef0d3051d560b4c2bcbdc6bb7d45db60. 

Basically, I am adding an empty path to all CR versions that don't have `scale`. The assumption is that manage fields entries won't ever have an empty path, so those entries just gets ignored [here](https://github.com/nodo/kubernetes/blob/scale-ownership-tracking-deployment/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/fieldmanager/scalehandler.go#L121-L124)
When would we not have the `requestInfo`?

FWIW this is what @liggitt linked earlier on: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/apps/deployment/strategy.go#L53-L56

I borrow the pattern from there. There are also some tests around different versions (see [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/34909133de6d5ae5786ff8f6e3dd697ddce75e71/pkg/registry/apps/daemonset/strategy_test.go#L43) ).

It's probably not exactly the same thing, so I am totally fine in changing the logic here.

That's great, I'm just curious how we would end-up with a `requestInfo` that doesn't know about a version we're serving here. Also I think we should rename `defaultGroupVersion` to merely `groupVersion` since default is a little misleading.
I have renamed the variable and cleaned up the commit history.
